categories.main_business_segments: Chubu Shiryo operates two main business segments: the 'Feed Segment,' which manufactures and sells livestock (chicken, pig, cattle) and aquaculture (fish) feed, and the 'Other Segment,' which includes sales of livestock and aquaculture products to consumers, sales of livestock equipment, production and sales of compound fertilizers, and insurance agency services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages integrated in-house production facilities for feed manufacturing, with a focus on developing differentiated and environmentally conscious feed products. R&D activities include the development of animal welfare-compliant feeds, feeds that reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and high-value-added aquaculture feeds using ingredients like herbs and brewer's yeast. The company also develops livestock waste fermentation equipment and compound fertilizers with organic content.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Chubu Shiryo primarily serves livestock and aquaculture producers, including poultry, swine, cattle, and fish farmers. Its end markets are the Japanese livestock and aquaculture industries, with some sales of finished livestock and aquaculture products to food retailers and consumers.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s operations are concentrated in Japan, with manufacturing and research facilities across Hokkaido, Tohoku, Kanto, Chubu, Chugoku, and Kyushu regions. It also has subsidiaries and affiliates in China (Jilin, Shandong, Dalian) and some overseas sales of livestock equipment and fertilizers.
categories.supply_chain_position: Chubu Shiryo operates primarily midstream in the supply chain, processing raw materials (mainly imported grains) into compound feed and supplying these to livestock and aquaculture producers. It also has downstream activities through the sale of finished livestock and aquaculture products and fertilizers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include strengthening profitability and scale in the feed segment, expanding differentiated and environmentally friendly feed products, and accelerating growth in the 'Other' segment (specialty eggs, fertilizers, livestock equipment, insurance). R&D focuses on sustainable feed development (e.g., low/zero fishmeal, methane-reducing feeds), resource recycling, and climate change adaptation, with a strong emphasis on ESG and sustainability.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through the sale of compound feed to livestock and aquaculture producers. Additional revenue streams include sales of livestock and aquaculture products, specialty eggs, fertilizers, livestock equipment, insurance agency commissions, and real estate leasing.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Chubu Shiryo is an independent, mid-sized comprehensive feed manufacturer in Japan, competing with larger integrated feed and food conglomerates such as NH Foods and Marubeni, as well as other domestic feed producers. It differentiates itself through its independent status, integrated production, and focus on specialty and environmentally friendly products.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated net sales were 209.8 billion yen, with operating profit of 4.28 billion yen and net profit attributable to parent company shareholders of 3.5 billion yen. The company has around 500 employees and maintains a stable financial base with a moderate growth profile, though sales declined 10.4% year-on-year due to lower average feed prices, while profits increased due to improved margins and growth in the 'Other' segment.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Chubu Shiryo emphasizes the stable supply of high-quality, safe, and tasty feed products that support the production of distinctive livestock and aquaculture products. Its unique value lies in its ability to develop and supply differentiated, environmentally conscious feeds and specialty products (e.g., 'Gomatamago' eggs, 'Imobuta' pork), as well as its commitment to sustainability and close partnership with producers.
